paper.title: Validity, Sparse Holes, and Breadth in Language Generation: Banach Density, Topology, and Geometry
paper.summary: Studies validity, sparse holes, and breadth through lower Banach density, containment topology, finite Cantor--Bendixson rank, and finite-tree geometry.

formalization_scope.summary: The complete selected-result inventory covers the four headline Banach-density and geometry theorems, the f-window dichotomy, the higher-dimensional discrepancy ingredient, and the principal structural claims. The structural density, topology, finite-rank, and finite-tree results are complete at their stated interfaces; the paper's dynamic generation and higher-dimensional conclusions are registered with zero Lean coverage rather than omitted.
specializations: One-dimensional densities are valued in extended nonnegative reals so nested infima are total.
Cantor--Bendixson ranks are formalized only at finite natural-number levels.
Claim 4.20 uses Mathlib predecessor-tree assumptions that make ancestor chains comparable.
gaps: Theorems 4.1, 4.5, 5.1, 5.5, 5.8, and 5.9 are registered but remain unformalized; the bridge from static structural trees to the dynamic pullback/pod state machine is absent.
Relative density, transfinite Cantor--Bendixson ranks, the infinite-rank hard family, discrepancy, and higher-dimensional geometry are not formalized.
The paper has no Results/Overview.lean facade; cards link canonical proof modules.

audit_refs.scope: Direct AI-assisted comparison of the thirteen selected headline and structural result groups against the SHA-256-pinned arXiv v2 PDF, including numbering defects, the finite-rank repair, and unformalized dynamic and geometric results; no human certification is claimed.
Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for every claim-linked P23 declaration.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Thirteen source-centered headline and structural groups: Overview Theorems 2.2--2.5 with their detailed counterparts, the f-window and size-sensitive-discrepancy results, and Claims 3.3, 3.5, 3.6, 4.4/7.1, 4.11, 4.18, and 4.20.
exclusions: Definitions are represented through the corresponding result cards and the PaperMap rather than separate theorem cards.
Theorem 4.8 is a restatement of the P07 accurate-selector theorem and remains represented by the P07 card rather than duplicated as a P23-owned result.
Claims 4.9, 4.13, 4.16, 4.23--4.25, 5.11, 5.13, Corollary 4.26, and supporting lemmas are proof infrastructure rather than independently selected headline cards.
Appendix Theorem 7.4 is grouped conceptually with the size-sensitive discrepancy card; textbook and proof-only appendix facts are excluded.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete is relative to the paper's headline results plus the independently reusable structural claims already exposed by Lean. Overview and detailed restatements are grouped; shared topology implementations remain Lean links rather than duplicate source cards.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: Canonical density, topology, nice-schedule, finite-rank, and finite-tree endpoints linked from the thirteen selected source groups.
exclusions: Definitions and proof-only window-count, derivative, and LCA helper lemmas.

claims.title: Lower Banach density is the smallest lower window density
claims.statement_summary: For every admissible nondecreasing window bound f, the one-dimensional lower Banach density is at most the corresponding lower f-window density.

source_assessment.notes: Lean uses extended nonnegative reals so every nested infimum is total; finite nonzero window ratios agree with the source's real-valued ratios.

formalization.notes: Lean packages the source inequality as the equivalent identity saying that lower Banach density is the infimum over admissible bounds, attained by the constant-top bound.

lean_links.notes: The constant WithTop infinity bound supplies the attaining witness.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for Claim 3.5.

claims.title: Limit points are exactly terminal languages of perfect towers
claims.statement_summary: A language is a limit point of the finite-containment topology exactly when it is the terminal language of an infinite perfect tower.

source_assessment.notes: The source states a pure topological equivalence; Lean supplies an exact presentation of the terminal language to construct the countable neighborhood basis used in the converse.

formalization.notes: Both directions reuse the neutral TowerTopology implementation shared with P07.

lean_links.notes: The P23 theorem is source-facing; its proof delegates to shared Support.KleinbergWei infrastructure.

relations.notes: P07 Claim 6.1 and P23 Claim 3.6 expose the same shared perfect-tower characterization under renamed paper numbering.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for Claim 3.6.

claims.title: Convergent sequences eventually have lower Cantor--Bendixson rank
claims.statement_summary: If a language K is the limit point of a convergent language sequence, then all sufficiently late terms of the sequence have Cantor--Bendixson rank strictly smaller than K.

source_assessment.notes: The source omits the proper/distinct sequence hypothesis; without it the constant sequence is a counterexample. Lean states the required premise explicitly.

formalization.notes: The derivative-exit argument and rank extraction are complete for natural-number Cantor--Bendixson ranks.

lean_links.notes: The properness premise rules out the constant-sequence counterexample.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for the repaired Claim 4.11 endpoint.

claims.title: Strict prefix-LCA changes are bounded by tree depth
claims.statement_summary: Along a finite-tree vertex sequence, the indices at which the prefix least common ancestor changes strictly have cardinality at most the tree depth bound.

source_assessment.notes: Lean isolates the finite order-theoretic tree invariant from the later dynamic construction.

formalization.notes: The exact cardinality form is derived from a monotone ancestral-chain invariant.

lean_links.notes: The theorem exposes the source's literal cardinality conclusion and generalizes the rooted-tree proof to any meet-semilattice carrying a strictly monotone natural depth bounded at the initial vertex.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for Claim 4.18.

claims.title: An adjacent ordered pair realizes the global LCA
claims.statement_summary: For an ordered list of at least two vertices in a rooted predecessor tree, some adjacent pair has least common ancestor equal to the LCA of the whole list.

source_assessment.notes: The source explicitly assumes a rooted tree. Lean represents that tree property with predecessor-order assumptions; failure in an arbitrary meet-semilattice is therefore not a defect in the paper claim.

formalization.notes: The adjacent-pair witness theorem is complete under the explicit rooted-tree interface.

lean_links.notes: The explicit tree assumptions are exactly what fails in the standard three-set meet-semilattice counterexample.

relations.notes: Both isolate static finite-tree geometry used by the later dynamic construction.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for Claim 4.20.

claims.title: Larger windows can only decrease lower window density
claims.statement_summary: If two admissible window bounds satisfy f(n) <= g(n) pointwise, then the lower g-window density of every language is at most its lower f-window density.

source_assessment.notes: The Lean inequality has the same direction and hypotheses as the source statement.

formalization.notes: The source monotonicity claim has a direct Lean theorem.

lean_links.notes: The extended-nonnegative-real codomain makes all infima total without changing the finite window ratios.

relations.notes: Claim 3.5 identifies the infimum over the densities ordered by this monotonicity principle.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for Claim 3.3.

claims.title: Nice window functions are exactly the unbounded ones
claims.statement_summary: An admissible window function admits a sequence of sufficiently separated scales with increasing window sizes exactly when it is unbounded.

source_assessment.notes: Claim 7.1 supplies the appendix proof of the characterization stated as Claim 4.4.

formalization.notes: Lean exposes both the main-text characterization and its appendix form.

relations.notes: The hard-family construction applies to every unbounded, equivalently nice, window function.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist audit for Claims 4.4 and 7.1.

claims.title: Every unbounded window scale has a countable zero-density hard class
claims.statement_summary: For every unbounded window function f, there is a countable language collection for which every valid generator has lower f-window density zero on some target; the result yields the Banach-density and finite-output-speed corollaries.

source_assessment.notes: The overview and detailed statements agree; the corollaries specialize the unbounded-window obstruction.

formalization.notes: The static window and topology interfaces are available, but the source's infinite-rank adversarial presentation is not formalized.

relations.notes: The construction uses the nice subsequence available exactly for unbounded f.

claims.title: Finite Cantor--Bendixson rank gives the optimal one-half guarantee
claims.statement_summary: For a countable language collection of finite Cantor--Bendixson rank and every unbounded window function, a valid generator attains lower f-window density at least one half; Banach-density and reordering corollaries follow.

source_assessment.notes: The published proof invokes the repaired proper-tower version of Claim 4.11; the PaperMap records why the printed unrestricted Claim 4.11 is false.

formalization.notes: Lean formalizes the corrected rank-drop and finite-tree ingredients, but not the paper's dynamic pullback/pod generator or its density proof.

relations.notes: The proof needs eventual strict rank drop along proper convergent towers.
The dynamic argument uses the finite bound on strict prefix-LCA changes.
The adjacent-pair LCA witness is part of the finite-tree geometry used by the construction.

claims.title: Rectangular Banach density can vanish in every dimension at least two
claims.statement_summary: For every dimension d at least two there is a single known target language such that, against every generator, the adversary can enumerate that target so the output has ordinary rectangular lower Banach density zero.

source_assessment.notes: The detailed display appears to put the target intersection inside the growth premise. The overview, definition, and surrounding prose use the intended premise that the rectangle size tends to infinity; this card records that reading.

formalization.notes: The higher-dimensional rectangle geometry is outside the current Lean development.

claims.title: Filtered higher-dimensional generation attains one half at finite rank
claims.statement_summary: For a finite-rank countable language collection, every dimension and every positive epsilon admit a valid generator whose target-filtered rectangular lower density is at least one half minus epsilon; Banach and finite-output-speed corollaries follow.

source_assessment.notes: Later prose calls the main result Theorem 5.6 although it is numbered 5.5, and Corollary 5.7 says identifies where the stated task is generation; the mathematical statements are otherwise coherent.

formalization.notes: Neither the filtered rectangular density interface nor the dynamic generator and discrepancy argument has been formalized.

relations.notes: The proof uses the size-sensitive discrepancy coloring theorem.

claims.title: Anchored higher-dimensional density admits a universal one-half guarantee
claims.statement_summary: For every dimension and every countable language collection, there is a valid generator whose anchored rectangular asymptotic lower density on each target is at least one half.

source_assessment.notes: The theorem is a separate anchored-density positive result, not a restatement of the filtered Banach-density theorem.

formalization.notes: The anchored higher-dimensional density interface and construction are not represented in Lean.

relations.notes: Both give one-half guarantees in higher dimensions under different density notions and hypotheses.

claims.title: Multi-level size-sensitive discrepancy for axis-parallel rectangles
claims.statement_summary: For every possibly infinite point set in the integer lattice, epsilon in (0,1), and positive filtration exponent, there is one global two-coloring whose discrepancy on every axis-parallel rectangle obeys the theorem's simultaneous size- and sparsity-tier bound.

source_assessment.notes: Appendix Theorem 7.4 states the Lovasz Local Lemma used in the finite-window argument before the coloring is extended to the possibly infinite point set.

formalization.notes: This probabilistic discrepancy theorem would require substantial finite-probability and concentration infrastructure not currently present in the paper package.

relations.notes: The coloring theorem is the principal combinatorial ingredient of the filtered higher-dimensional generation result.
